---
title: "check-definition-expectation.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only heuristic check for the lab's rule
(Ezra, 2026-11-07; psw#513)
to write a definition with an expectation operator where one fits:
`\E{\log \frac{1}{p(X)}}`, not `\sum_x p(x) \log \frac{1}{p(x)}`.

The check flags a `#def-` div when both conditions hold:

- A display equation contains a sum or an integral,
  and the summand is a probability mass or density
  (`p(x)`, `p_X(x)`, `f(x)`, `f_X(x)`, or `\Pr(...)`) times another factor.
- The div holds no expectation operator
  (`\E`, `\Exp`, `\Expect`, `\mathbb{E}`, `\mathrm{E}`, or `\operatorname{E}`).

It skips

- a display with a `\frac{1}{n}` factor, or a sum over a data index from 1 to `n`,
  which is a sample average;
- a lone mass or density, such as `\sum_x p(x) = 1`, which weights nothing; and
- a div titled "Expectation" or "Expected value", which defines the operator itself.

A definition that holds `<!-- check-definition-expectation: allow -->` is exempt.

A definition is checked when the pull request adds a line inside it.
With no base to diff against,
the check skips instead of scanning the whole tree.
It only warns by default,
because whether an expectation expresses the quantity needs judgement.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | `*.qmd` | Git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive) |
| `paths-ignore` | none | Comma or newline separated globs to skip |
| `fail` | `false` | Fail on a finding; `false` warns |
| `whole-tree` | `false` | Check every definition, to measure a corpus |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version |
| `runs-on` | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label; a self-hosted label only for a private repository |

## Usage

Copy `examples/check-definition-expectation.yml` to
`.github/workflows/check-definition-expectation.yml`.
